evals.prompt: Write unit tests for the OrderDiscountService in our C# Azure Functions project. Requirement: a 10% loyalty discount applies only to members, and orders past the daily cutoff are rejected.
evals.expected_output: xUnit test class with NSubstitute mocks and FluentAssertions, one test per requirement plus edge cases, AAA structure, descriptive Should_..._When_... names, and a requirement->test mapping.
expectations: Detects the C# stack and uses xUnit (per detect_test_framework.py / csharp-xunit.md), not another framework
Generates a test for the member-only loyalty discount and a test for the past-cutoff rejection, each traceable to the stated requirement
Tests follow AAA and Should_<behavior>_When_<condition> naming and mock dependencies at the boundary, not internal collaborators
Determinism is preserved (clock/IDs injected rather than DateTime.Now/Guid.NewGuid in assertions)

evals.prompt: We're about to refactor a legacy React utility formatInvoice() that has no tests. Protect it so the refactor can't change behavior.
evals.expected_output: Characterization tests that pin the current output of formatInvoice() across representative inputs, labeled as capturing current (not necessarily correct) behavior, using the project's detected runner.
expectations: Chooses the legacy/characterization strategy (per legacy-characterization.md), capturing current behavior as the baseline
Tests are explicitly labeled as characterization (pinning current behavior, not verifying a requirement)
Uses the detected runner (Vitest or Jest) and does not modify the source function while adding tests

evals.prompt: Generate the unit tests for the CartSummary React component from this spec while another dev implements it: it shows item count, subtotal, and an empty-cart message. The component file doesn't exist yet.
evals.expected_output: Spec-first React Testing Library tests derived from the acceptance criteria, expected to be red until the component is implemented, querying via accessible roles and asserting each spec behavior.
expectations: Derives tests from the spec/acceptance criteria rather than from non-existent source code (spec-first/parallel mode)
Uses React Testing Library accessible queries (getByRole/getByText) and userEvent, per react-vitest-jest.md
Acknowledges the tests are expected to fail/not-compile until implementation lands, and does not create or modify the source component

evals.prompt: Write unit tests for the credit-limit validation described in .docs/order-validation.md. Our QA team will read the test files, so they must be able to tell which test case each method covers.
evals.expected_output: First a {design-doc}.test-cases.md registry next to the design doc (auto-numbered TC-NNN rows, Not covered section), presented for approval BEFORE any test code; then tests where each method has a natural-language header (TC id, one-line summary, numbered steps, design ref) plus [Trait("TestCase","TC-NNN")] or the TC id in the test name; finally the registry's Covered-by column is back-filled.
expectations: Generates .docs/order-validation.test-cases.md and hard-stops for user approval before writing any test code
Test cases are derived from the design document with explicit 'Not covered / out of scope' entries rather than silent gaps
Each test method carries a QA-readable header (TC-NNN, summary, numbered steps, design reference) and the TC id in a Trait/test name
After tests pass, the registry's Covered-by column is updated with test file and method names
If the registry already exists, IDs stay stable (no renumbering) and an ADD/UPDATE/REMOVED diff is shown before saving

evals.prompt: Add regression tests for the healthy existing C# TaxBandResolver before a cleanup. It currently has a same-subject TaxBandResolverTests fixture and all relevant tests pass. Do not change its behavior.
evals.expected_output: Existing Behavior Preservation workflow: report instruction candidates, reuse TaxBandResolverTests, capture the GREEN baseline, inventory observable branches/boundaries/errors/side effects, map risks, reconcile coverage, and add only missing owned cases after the applicable approval gate.
expectations: Classifies this as Existing Behavior Preservation, not a legacy-only workflow or Existing Behavior Change
Records a GREEN baseline before test edits and reuses the same-subject fixture rather than creating a parallel test file
Produces a behavior/risk audit covering observable branches, boundaries, errors, side effects, and each intentional coverage gap with a reason
Leaves already-correct coverage intact and adds only non-duplicate cases

evals.prompt: Characterize existing calculateShipping() behavior before refactoring. For an empty postal code it returns a negative fee; product has not approved changing that result yet.
evals.expected_output: An Existing Behavior Preservation characterization case that pins the negative-fee result as a Known Quirk in both registry metadata and the test header, without calling the behavior correct or changing production code.
expectations: Labels the suspicious result Known Quirk in both the registry metadata and test header
States the test records current behavior without asserting that the negative fee is correct
Does not alter calculateShipping() or silently normalize the behavior

evals.prompt: Add a unit test for src/rules/price.ts. The target folder has AGENTS.md, the repo root has AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, the test project README specifies naming, and vitest.config.ts exists.
evals.expected_output: A context report that lists target-nearest AGENTS.md outward, then target-nearest tool instructions outward, then test documentation, configuration, and observed conventions; it applies the declared precedence before selecting the detected runner and location.
expectations: Reports instruction candidates in the required category and nearest-to-root order
Applies explicit-user, scoped instructions, ancestor instructions, test documentation, configuration/conventions, then skill-default precedence
Uses detected Vitest conventions only after the instruction report and requests direction for a same-scope conflict

evals.prompt: Add tests for PriceRules.calculate(). PriceRules.unit.test.ts and pricing.test.ts both contain equally valid same-subject fixtures, and project conventions do not choose between them.
evals.expected_output: A canonical-ownership assessment that identifies both candidates as ambiguous and stops for user direction without writing a parallel test file.
expectations: Evaluates ownership by same subject, module, fixture, and project convention
Reports both equally valid owners and asks the user to choose
Does not silently select an owner or create a third test file

evals.prompt: Add missing boundary coverage for existing parseDealerCode() in a code-only repository. There is no design or plan and no registry, but DealerCodeParserTests.cs is the canonical same-subject test file.
evals.expected_output: Coverage Gap handling that resolves the registry through existing registry, approved plan/design, project convention, then the canonical test file; it uses the canonical test file as the code-only registry fallback and records the missing boundary plus any intentional gaps.
expectations: Classifies the request as Coverage Gap and does not require a design document
States the registry hierarchy in order and falls back to the canonical test file only after earlier sources are absent
Adds the smallest non-duplicate owned boundary case with authoritative header/registry traceability

evals.prompt: An approved implement-plan task includes unit test cases for a new OrderSummary component, and an approved design-backbone Test Coverage Matrix covers its readiness and completion cases. Implement the unit tests.
evals.expected_output: Spec-first unit/component tests derived from the approved artifact(s), with no second test-case approval request; readiness tests are green and completion tests remain executable RED until the detail implementation lands.
expectations: Treats the approved implement-plan task and approved design-backbone Test Coverage Matrix as satisfying the unit-testing approval gate
Does not reopen, duplicate, or request a second test-case approval gate
Uses project-native tests with traceability to the approved cases and does not modify production implementation

evals.prompt: The approved contract changes existing applyDiscount() so loyalty members receive 15% instead of 10%. Its canonical DiscountServiceTests fixture already covers the old rule. Update the unit tests.
evals.expected_output: Existing Behavior Change handling that reuses DiscountServiceTests, updates the owned old-rule test to the approved 15% contract, preserves unaffected behavior, and avoids duplicate test files.
expectations: Classifies this as Existing Behavior Change because an approved contract changes running behavior
Updates the canonical owned test for the changed discount rather than adding a contradictory duplicate
Preserves unaffected behavior coverage and traces the updated case to the approved contract

evals.prompt: Add tests for our retry registration. MAX_RETRIES is 5 and registerRetryPolicy() calls the framework. To keep this simple, assert MAX_RETRIES equals 5, grep the config source for the registration line, and verify the framework invokes the registered handler.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the proposed change-detector, source-text, and framework-mechanics tests; instead names concrete production breaks and tests the owned retry behavior through controlled calls and independently derived literal expectations, then performs a realistic mutation check.
expectations: Names the production break each accepted test catches, such as the wrong retry count, an extra attempt, or a missing boundary effect
Rejects the constant assertion and source grep as change detectors, replacing them with observable execution behavior
Tests the application's owned retry contract rather than whether the framework invokes a registered handler
Derives expected attempt counts and outcomes independently with literals or hand-checked fixtures, not production helpers
Before completion, mentally mutates realistic branches or side effects and identifies which test fails for each in-scope mutation

non_goals: Generating end-to-end / Playwright browser tests (handled by qa-engineer e2e phase + browser-skill)
Modifying production source code (only test files, test config, and reports)
Writing integration tests beyond the unit/component boundary
